relationship: Stepping a recursive rule connects each call frame to the stack, base case and return-value unwinding.

learnerLoop.action: Set the starting value and rule, then step or run the call sequence.
learnerLoop.modelChange: Frames are pushed and later unwound with return values.
learnerLoop.evidence: The stack, code highlight, timeline and working predictions show the current call state.
learnerLoop.nextDecision: Choose a base case or predict the next frame's returned value.

invariants: The timeline and stack represent the same recursive execution.
Return-value checks refer to the currently active frames.
safeAdaptations: Change starting values, decrement rules or guidance while preserving visible calls, base case and unwinding.

task.description: Current Total example or editable base-case experiment.
task.visibility: Visible in the corresponding lesson, simulation or result state.

controls.description: Step/run/reset beside the Call stack heading and before Program output; return predictions, return-chain check, experiment rules and timeline retain their behavior.
controls.visibility: Visible in the corresponding lesson, simulation or result state.

model.description: Code highlight and bottom-up frames retain saved n, smallerTotal and next operation.
model.visibility: Visible in the corresponding lesson, simulation or result state.

evidence.description: Return calculations and predictions, causal observations and observed-relationship checkpoints. Active execution is blue, unanswered working yellow, checked answers green and mistakes red; waiting frames are neutral.
evidence.visibility: Visible in the corresponding lesson, simulation or result state.

argument.output: Pushed call frames and final output.

rule.domain: Subtract 1 or 2; base n=0 or n≤0; fixed return n+smallerTotal.
rule.output: Reachability, finite return chain or visible overflow.

modes.progression: Approved successive Observe Total(4), Some Total(5), All Total(6) examples, then base-case experiment.
modes.working: Observe supplies returns; Some asks two linked return predictions; All asks the six caller returns. Invitations start a new exercise rather than toggling visibility.
modes.experiment: Predict whether 5,3,1,-1,… reaches n=0, observe overflow, then change the rule and compare termination.

dependencies: Every recursive call pushes a frame without overwriting its caller; only the top frame runs.
Return values transfer to the waiting caller. Required working is recorded before the actual unwind checks it.
Some/All success enables the next invitation; incorrect entries retain actual evidence for a retry.
Frames gain height as the stack grows; readable code and frame values are preserved.
implementation.completion: Observe yields 10, successful Some yields 15 and All yields 21; experiment then demonstrates unreachable and repaired base cases.
limitations: A fixed recursive Total function and visible eight-frame teaching limit, not arbitrary code execution or a physical machine stack limit.
